name: a bent rusty metal sheet, broken concrete lumps, glass shards and a torn cable lying on an oil-stained patch of earth
label: wasteland_ruins/rubble-c

surfaces.part: oil-stained earth patch (full tile, main body)
debris cluster (rusty sheet, concrete, glass, cable), upper right

answer.evidence: The tile is an opaque 64x48 patch of mottled brown earth with a uniform width of 64 on every row, so there is no silhouette, no front-edge line and no south face. The column scans at x=16, 32 and 47 show only earth texture with small debris runs. The three small clusters of sheet metal, concrete and glass are drawn from above as flat colour blobs with no front face or eave shadow. The whole thing is a ground decal seen from above, which fits the 'flat' kind. It has no front face of 3 or more rows, so it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The earth is mottled with several brown tones and speckle grain, so there are no large flat fills (2% near-flat, against 0% for both references). It shows 5 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7), so density is comparable to the references rather than much lower. Only 3% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean brown or red-brown rather than being a black sticker line. The weak points are that the debris clusters are small and look like near-repeats of one sprite, and the oil stain barely reads. The ramps are about 4 steps against the references' 5-6. Overall it is acceptable beside the references, if a little thin.
